summary: Ratna Basu is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989. As of 2026, she holds the post of Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society.

Ratna Handurukande, a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Harold Walter Bailey. She served as a lecturer at the University of Peradeniya and as a lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon (attested 1970).
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga as his traditional teacher and succeeded him in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford, he held teaching posts at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming Charles Redd Chair at Utah State University (~2013).

Ravi Prakash Arya is an Indologist who studied at Panjab University. He served in Haryana's Department of Higher Education (1993–2019), directed the Indian Foundation for Vedic Science (2019–2021), held a chair at Maharshi Dayanand University (2021–2025), and became President of Vedic Science Virtual Vishva Vidyapeeth in 2025.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Lucknow, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He worked in Punjab and Haryana state archaeology departments and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India until 2004.

Ravindra Suryakant Kale works in Indology and computational fields. He held library posts at IOCL, Mahila Mahavidyalaya, Prof. V. B. Shah Institute of Management, and Narmada College of Management before becoming Librarian at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University in 2014.

Ravinjay Kuckreja is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed a BA at the University of Chester (2014–2017), an MA at IE University (2017–2018), and a doctorate in religious studies at Universitas Hindu Negeri I Gusti Bagus Sugriwa (2020–2023).

Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Chulalongkorn University, University of Adelaide, and Australian National University, served as a physics professor at Chulalongkorn University (1945–1986), and was a fellow of the Royal Institute of Thailand (~1986–2017).
Ray Caldwell Smith was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at San Francisco Theological Seminary (~1897–1900) and held a post at the Landour Community Centre Language School.

Raymond Bloch was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, University of Paris, and École Pratique des Hautes Études, he worked at the École française de Rome, EPHE (1949–1983), and CNRS (1973–1983).

Raymond West was an Indologist educated at the University of Galway and under Martin Haug. He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1886–1892), and Reader at the University of Cambridge (1901–1907).
Raymonde Linossier was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist. She studied under Sylvain Lévi (~1920–1926) and served as an unsalaried attachée at the Guimet Museum in 1925.

Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies scholar and Zen practitioner. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker, whom he succeeded, and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center (~1986–1995).

Rebecca Hufen is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Attested in 2026 at the University of Hamburg, she works as a Tibetan Studies lector and conducts doctoral research supervised by Dorji Wangchuk.

Rebecca Manring is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied under Carol Salomon and Richard G. Salomon, and was appointed Associate Professor at Indiana University Bloomington in 1996.

Rebecca Redwood French is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. from Yale University. She held legal academic posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University at Buffalo.
Rebecca Sundén is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg, where she is attested in 2026 as a project researcher (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin).

Reginald A. Ray is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated under mentors including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa. He has taught at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).
Reginald Edward Enthoven was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at Wellington College (~1882–1887) and New College in 1887.
